blogs.title: When GLP‑1 Gets Muscular: Is Semaglutide a New Culprit for Immune‑Mediated Necrotising Myopathy?
blogs.description: Explore the emerging link between GLP‑1 receptor agonists and IMNM, reviewing pharmacodynamics, known muscle‑related adverse events, and how to suspect a drug‑induced myopathy in patients with rapid CK rises after a single dose.

blogs.title: Steroid‑Free or Short‑Course? A Practical Guide to Managing Drug‑Induced IMNM
blogs.description: Delve into the therapeutic algorithm for IMNM triggered by medications, contrasting it with idiopathic forms. Discuss the evidence for pulse methylprednisolone, oral taper, and the role of IVIG in early recovery—as illustrated by this patient’s rapid improvement.

blogs.title: From Nausea to Dysphagia: When a First‑Dose GI Reaction Signals a Beneath Myopathy
blogs.description: Analyze the diagnostic dilemma when a patient’s initial adverse effect (GI upset, renal insufficiency) precedes a long‑term progressive myopathy. Highlight the importance of serial CK monitoring, bedside exam, and early referral to rheumatology or neurology.

blogs.title: Autoantibody‐Negative Yet Autoimmune: The Challenge of Seronegative IMNM
blogs.description: Discuss the 30% of IMNM cases lacking HMGCR or SRP antibodies, including work‑up strategies, biopsy hallmarks, and why seronegative patients may respond differently to immunosuppression or may represent drug‑induced phenotypes.

blogs.title: Muscle and Metabolism: Considering Pre‑Existing Liver Disease and Muscle Inflammation
blogs.description: Examine how chronic NAFLD and mild transaminase elevations can confound the work‑up of a suspected myopathy, and why distinguishing hepatic from muscular causes of AST/ALT is crucial during clinical evaluation.

blogs.title: Pharmacovigilance in the Age of Obesity Drugs: How Case Reports Shape Safe Prescribing
blogs.description: Reflect on the role of individual case reports in detecting rare adverse events, the use of WHO‑UMC causality criteria, and practical steps clinicians can take to report and monitor for drug‑induced myopathies with GLP‑1 agents.
